newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama's leader urges country to prepare for WTO.
newsitem.headline: Panama's leader urges country to prepare for WTO.

text.p: Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares urged the producing sector to be more competitive when Panama joins the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
He told a news conference on Tuesday that lower tariffs would benefit national producers, not hurt them.
But he said "they have to understand that they have to be active, competitive and efficient" when the country applies for entry in the WTO on October 2.

"We are still talking about very high protection levels. They (WTO) are talking about maximum tariffs of 10 percent and minimum tariffs of 3 percent in almost all products. Most of our neighbours already have tariffs lower than we do," he said.

Panama ended trade negotiations on several sticking points with the European Union this summer. One of them was agriculture products. Panama agreed to open its market and reduce tariffs over 10 years. In the industrial sector, a 40 percent ceiling on tariffs would be imposed and would fall to 30 percent over five years.
The Geneva-based WTO replaced the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade which Panama said in 1991 it would seek to join. It began negotiations in December 1994.
